points.text: The group agrees to buy two more Crown microphones right away, since the Sony headsets pinch and are hard to adjust and the Crown mikes give a slightly better signal.
Speaker C plans four more wireless channels, pending a check with Morgan, and will likely swap the problematic wired Andrea mike for a Shure after testing it.
Compressing wave files with the Sphere Wencode shorten option is accepted as a good short-term fix for disk space, since it needs no coding.
In Speaker F's experiments the ICSI front-end gives about 52.6 and 51.3 percent error against about 49 and 47.1 for the SRI front-end; combining them gives 48.5 and 46.5.
Speaker D installed Transcriber and Channeltrans on an NT machine, so they are now available under Windows.
Speaker C asks people to write Crown or Sony in the mike type field, and whoever sets up the meeting fills out the key file.
Speaker C advises Speaker D to ask a Sys Admin to put Transcriber in a central place for all NT machines, and Speaker D agrees.
Speaker B and Speaker E have not yet read the naming conventions Speaker C sent; Speaker E will read them by next week.
Speaker C wants a list of file reorganization tasks drawn up, and Speaker B suggests doing that next week.
Speaker C says a check is needed on why the backup software sees the same meeting files as rewritten every night, since Dave Johnson has not yet looked into it.
Speaker F does not want the segment names changed without advance notice, and Speaker A is also reluctant to rename everything; this is not settled.
How to prevent meetings being recorded with microphones off is unresolved; Speaker C says dead channels are detectable, but what the software should do is not decided.
Speaker B asks whether a NIST routine can seek in a compressed file with uncompressed indices; Speaker F does not think so.
The group covers microphone purchases, file reorganization and disk space, a Windows Transcriber install, recognition experiment results, and then reads digits.
The EDU group dislikes the Crown mikes, but several speakers here prefer them, and Speaker C says they sound slightly better than the Sony ones.
Speaker F proposes compressing files with Wencode shorten to save disk space, and describes gaining three gigabytes this way during a Switchboard-two run.
A disk crash and odd nightly backup activity on wave files raise questions about how files are spread across disks.
Speaker D installed Transcriber and Channeltrans on an NT machine.
The ICSI front-end performs worse than the SRI front-end, but combining the two still improves the error rate.
Speaker F raises that some meetings were recorded with microphones off, and the group considers ways to catch this.
The group will buy two more Crown mikes and track mike type in the key file.
The group will make a list of file reorganization and naming changes, possibly next week.
Speaker F will run the SRI system without vocal tract length normalization as a diagnostic.
Speaker F and Chuck built a script that runs ICSI feature calculation and writes the cepstra files the SRI system reads.

Speaker F trained male and female ICSI-feature systems plus an SRI-feature baseline, with comparable configuration, and got error rates of about 52.6 and 51.3 percent for ICSI versus 49 and 47.1 for SRI.
Combining the two systems at utterance level gives 48.5 and 46.5 percent error, so combination still helps.
Speaker D installed Transcriber and Channeltrans on an NT machine.
Speaker F attributes about one percent of the ICSI gap to missing vocal tract length normalization, and Czero normalization differs between the systems.
The gap widens with adaptation, and the combination gain shrinks.
Disk space is tight, and a disk crash left channel files split across disks and disorganized.
The backup software sees the same shortened meeting files as rewritten nightly, which is unexplained.
Some meetings were recorded with several microphones turned off, which makes them unusable.
Speaker C will test a Shure mike today or tomorrow to replace the Andrea mike.
Chuck is working on tandem features, and Speaker F is retraining on the large training set and plans system combination, probably on males only.
Speaker F will run the SRI system without vocal tract length normalization, and may try warping factors with the ICSI front-end.
Speaker C plans to get two more Crown mikes and four more wireless channels.
The group will buy two more Crown mikes now and plans four more wireless channels, after the EDU group's dislike of the Crown headsets.
File reorganization and naming conventions need a task list, with shortening files as the short-term disk-space fix.
The ICSI front-end trails the SRI front-end in error rate, but combining the two still helps.
